notes: v2 (26 Sep 2026 review): removed 'reputation' (not a resource in scope doc 10); every effect now uses a scope resource or a named modifier. 'requires' hides a choice or card when the condition is false. String effects are resolver expressions: whitelist them or convert to {op,var,mult} objects in the Zod schema.

effect_vocabulary.heat: change to Community Heat at the affected site (all sites if no site context)
effect_vocabulary.heat_base: permanent change to a site's base Heat
effect_vocabulary.machines / machines_used: add units {model_id: count} at current new/used price, unless cash effect says otherwise
effect_vocabulary.sell_treasury_pct: sell share of treasury at this week's price
effect_vocabulary.hashrate_mult: multiplier on affected fleet for duration_weeks or duration_quarters
effect_vocabulary.failure_mult: multiplier on failure chance for the rest of the quarter unless a duration is given
effect_vocabulary.power_price_mult: multiplier on the site's power price from next quarter
effect_vocabulary.machines_used_discount: used machines cost (1 - x) for the rest of the quarter
effect_vocabulary.gpu_purchase_lock_quarters: no new GPU purchases for N quarters
effect_vocabulary.site_expansion_lock_quarters: no capacity added at this site for N quarters
effect_vocabulary.loans_locked_quarters: no new loans of any kind for N quarters
effect_vocabulary.unlock / flag: turns on an action, interrupt or story flag
effect_vocabulary.success_p / on_success / on_failure: resolves a gamble with the seeded RNG

events.title: Graphics Cards: Sold Out
events.body: Every shop has the same sign: no RX 580s, no ETA. A forum seller will ship six cards at 60% over list. Gamers are furious. Your spreadsheet is delighted.

choices.label: Pay the markup for one rig

events.real_basis: May–Aug 2017: RX 470/480/580 and GTX 1060/1070 sold out; ETH rose from ~$8 to ~$400 in H1 2017

events.title: Nineteen Thousand
events.body: Bitcoin touches $19,000. Your barber asks about wallets. Your cousin wants to quit his job to mine. Everyone agrees it can only go up.

choices.label: Buy more machines at today's prices

events.real_basis: BTC ~$19.5k on 17 Dec 2017, then ~$6.9k on 6 Feb 2018 (−65%). The crash itself is a market shock and a price-alert interrupt, not a second card

events.title: Capitulation
events.body: Network hashrate is falling for the first time in years. Farms are dumping S9s by the container. With ETH at $85, most garage rigs now lose money every night.

choices.label: Go shopping in the fire sale
Sell half the rigs while anyone still buys

events.real_basis: BTC low ~$3,200 (15 Dec 2018); difficulty fell ~15% on 3 Dec 2018; ETH ~$84

events.title: The Other Use for GPUs
events.body: An old contact says a small ETH farm in New Jersey is quietly renting its cards to render studios and AI researchers. 'Better margin than mining,' he claims. Nobody else seems interested.
events.real_basis: Atlantic Crypto (founded 2017) began offering GPU compute in 2019 and renamed itself CoreWeave
events.design_note: cloud_insight adds a one-line hint to the gpu_cloud option on the Merge screen

events.title: Black Thursday
events.body: Markets everywhere are selling everything. Bitcoin drops 40% in a day. The next difficulty adjustment is two weeks away, and every S9 on the network is suddenly underwater.

choices.label: Sell half the treasury to protect cash

events.real_basis: 12–13 Mar 2020: BTC ~$7.9k → ~$4.9k; difficulty −16% on 26 Mar 2020

events.title: The Third Halving
events.body: Block 630,000. The reward drops from 12.5 to 6.25 BTC overnight. Anything less efficient than the new S19 is now a space heater with opinions.

choices.label: Sell every S9 and move to S19 Pros
Keep the S9s where power is cheapest

events.real_basis: 11 May 2020; hashprice fell ~45–50%

events.title: Winter Storm Uri
events.body: Texas freezes. Grid prices hit the $9,000/MWh cap. The grid operator asks large loads to shut down. At your contract price, the power you are not using is worth more than the bitcoin you would mine.

choices.label: Curtail and sell the power back

events.real_basis: 15–19 Feb 2021 ERCOT load shed; price at the $9,000/MWh cap for ~4 days
events.design_note: Payout = 2.5× the week's forgone mining revenue (real Uri resale value was ~14×; capped so it isn't a lottery win, flag F9). Example: 40 MW of S19s in Feb 2021 forgo ~$2.5M, so curtailing pays ~$6.3M.

events.title: Everyone Wants a Miner
events.body: Bankers call daily. Two blank-check companies want to merge with you at 'thirty times forward EBITDA'. Bitcoin makes a new all-time high. The window is open. Nobody knows for how long.
events.real_basis: Record SPAC issuance in Q1 2021; BTC passed $60k on 13 Mar 2021; miner listings followed through 2021 (Cipher, Greenidge, Stronghold, IREN, TeraWulf; Core Scientific in Jan 2022)
events.design_note: Moved from 2021Q4 to 2021Q1 so it opens the IPO window instead of arriving at its end. The Nov 2021 ATH stays as a market shock + news item.

events.title: The Great Migration
events.body: China orders miners to shut down. Half the world's hashrate goes dark within weeks. Container ships full of S19s head for Texas and Kazakhstan. Every machine still running just got a much bigger slice of the rewards.

choices.label: Buy exiled machines at a discount
Rent spare racks to an exiled miner

events.real_basis: State Council statement 21 May 2021; Sichuan shutdowns Jun 2021; hashrate ~180 → ~85 EH/s; difficulty −28% on 3 Jul 2021 (hashprice up ~35% the following week)

events.title: Contagion
events.body: A $40B stablecoin melted in three days. Now a big crypto lender has 'paused withdrawals'. Every lender in the space wants its collateral back, today.

choices.label: Repay crypto loans from the treasury
Sell half the treasury before it falls further

events.real_basis: Terra/LUNA collapse 9–13 May 2022; Celsius froze withdrawals 12 Jun 2022; BTC low ~$17.6k on 18 Jun
events.design_note: Moved to the Celsius week (was the Luna week). Crypto-backed loans close after this quarter.

events.title: Smoke in the Rack
events.body: A PDU overheats at 3 a.m. The sprinklers work. So does the insurance, eventually.
events.real_basis: Mining farm fires, e.g. Bitmain Mianning (Oct 2018) and hosted US sites

events.title: The Building Is Sold
events.body: Your landlord has sold the building to a self-storage chain. You have one quarter to move, or to make the buyer an offer.
events.real_basis: Short-lease miners displaced by building sales and rezoning, upstate NY and Quebec 2018 (≈)

events.title: Customs Hold
events.body: Your ASICs are sitting at Long Beach. Customs has reclassified them under the new China tariffs. Pay the duty or wait for a ruling.
events.real_basis: USTR Section 301 List 3 tariffs on Chinese goods (Sep 2018, 10% → 25% in 2019); CBP classification disputes over ASICs 2021

events.title: Moratorium Vote
events.body: The council votes 4–1 for an 18-month pause on new mining load. Existing machines may keep running. Your expansion may not.
events.real_basis: Plattsburgh NY moratorium, 15 Mar 2018

events.title: Missing Inventory
events.body: The side door was open. Four rigs are gone. The police officer asks what a hashrate is.

choices.label: Take the loss and install security

events.real_basis: Mining rig thefts, e.g. ~600 machines stolen in Iceland (Dec 2017–Jan 2018)

events.title: Too Good to Be True
events.body: A seller offers S19s at half the market price. Bank transfer only, 'shipping from Shenzhen'.
events.real_basis: Fake ASIC reseller sites and deposit scams, 2021

events.title: New Rate Class
events.body: The utility creates a 'high-density load' tariff. It applies to exactly one kind of customer.
events.real_basis: Chelan County PUD 2018–19; Hydro-Québec crypto tariff 2019

events.title: Heat Dome
events.body: Forty-two degrees outside, forty-eight inside. Hashboards are dropping one after another.
events.real_basis: Texas summer 2022 heat reduced miner uptime; ERCOT conservation calls Jul 2022

events.title: A Friend Calls
events.body: One of your early backers is buying a flat. They'd like their $15,000 back. They're sure you understand.
events.real_basis: Anecdotal: friends-and-family redemptions in crypto winters

events.title: Mined Coins Are Income
events.body: Your accountant explains that every coin you mined was taxable income on the day you mined it. Including the ones now worth half that.
events.real_basis: IRS Notice 2014-21: mined crypto is ordinary income at fair market value on receipt

market_phases.note: Used by 'market_phase==winter' triggers; all other quarters are 'normal'
